original_question: When one decomposes the graded tensor-product representations built for PB and PF, do irreducible components appear beyond the known p-Fock-like modules? In other words, can these decompositions produce direct summands or more general submodules that are not equivalent to the standard p-Fock-like representations?
target_in_paper: Section 4.2 ('Description of the Problem–Research Objectives'), especially the sentence asking whether the irreducible decomposition of the graded tensor-product representations can yield 'direct summands or more generally ... submodules' that are non-equivalent to the p-Fock-like module; this is foreshadowed almost verbatim by the final bullet of Section 4.1.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the paper's central open issue in this part very well: it is indeed about decomposing the graded tensor-product representations arising in the braided construction, acknowledging that the standard order-p Fock-like module already appears there, and asking whether additional inequivalent constituents can also occur, either as irreducible summands or more general submodules.
missing_details: The paper works over the field of complex numbers ℂ, and it explicitly uses 'module' as synonymous with 'representation'.
PB and PF should be identified as the free parabosonic and free parafermionic algebras introduced in Section 2.
The scope here is the infinite-degree-of-freedom case for PB and PF, not an arbitrary finite-generator truncation.

The relevant objects are not arbitrary graded tensor-product representations: they are the specific p-fold Z_2-graded tensor-product representations produced by the Section 4 braided method from suitably graded CCR/CAR modules.
The parameter p is a fixed but arbitrary positive integer; the known constituent is the standard order-p Fock-like module.
For PB, the construction is obtained by pulling back along suitable homogeneous homomorphisms built from the braided comultiplication; your draft omits this constructional origin.

The paper's exact previously known result is that the p-Fock-like module is contained as an irreducible factor/direct summand of the constructed graded tensor-product representation; the open problem is whether anything inequivalent appears in addition.

The paper phrases the question specifically after decomposing those constructed graded tensor-product representations into irreducible components; your draft does not explicitly restrict the question to that decomposition problem.
For PF, the paper presents the analogous problem as apparently easier because the relevant tensor-product variables appear commuting; your draft does not mention this asymmetry.
No homogeneity degree, polynomial degree, or nilpotency hypothesis is part of this open problem; the issue is purely representation-theoretic within the braided tensor-product construction.
refined_question: Over ℂ, fix a positive integer p. In the Section 4 braided construction for the infinite-degree free parabosonic algebra P_B—and analogously for the free parafermionic algebra P_F—one forms p-fold Z_2-graded tensor-product representations from suitably graded CCR/CAR modules (for P_B, via the homogeneous maps induced by the braided comultiplication), and it is already known that the standard order-p Fock-like module occurs as an irreducible factor. When these graded tensor-product representations are decomposed into irreducible components, is the standard p-Fock-like module the only constituent up to equivalence, or can there also appear additional direct summands, or at least submodules, carrying representations inequivalent to the standard p-Fock-like module?
justification: The draft is essentially a close paraphrase of the open question stated at the end of the first research-objective paragraph in Section 4.2, p. 85, where the author asks whether the graded CCR/CAR tensor-product decompositions can produce non-equivalent representations beyond the p-Fock-like ones already known to occur. The same issue is stated slightly earlier, in the paper's most programmatic form, in the final bullet of Section 4.1 on pp. 84–85. To make the question stand alone, one must restore the paper's ambient conventions (over ℂ, module = representation), the fact that PB and PF are the free parabosonic/parafermionic algebras from Section 2, the infinite-degree-of-freedom scope, the fixed arbitrary positive integer p, and the specific braided p-fold graded tensor-product construction from suitably graded CCR/CAR modules.
